And they made peace only until the harvest,
so that they might give up the crop.
And in this same year,
certain Frankish Genoese also attacked many ships of the Arabs which were coming from the cities of Tinnis and Damietta,
and they took captive seventy Arab merchants,
and sold them for large sums.
And they took from them four hundred chests of Egyptian sugar,
and fifty loads of Damietta fabrics and other goods.
And at this time a certain jurist (faqih) from the people of Aleppo came to Baghdad,
weeping and uttering lamentations over Islam,
which had suffered defeat at the hands of the Franks.
And the common people gathered together, and on Friday they entered their Great Mosque,
and broke the minbar, that is, the pulpit,
and stopped the prayer,
while murmuring against the Caliph and against the Sultan because they did not show zeal on behalf of their religion.
Now when the Sultan heard these things,
he made ready Abu'l-Fath Mas'ud his son and the Emir Mawdud with a large army,
and sent them to Mosul,
so that they might prepare for war with the Franks.
And in the year 1422
[1422] of the Greeks, the atabeg of the Sultan of Melitene took the region of Jihan from the Franks.
And in the year 505
[505] of the Arabs,
the Emir Mawdud, the lord of Mosul, went to Syria with a large army.
And on his way he conquered certain fortresses in the region of Shabakhtan,
and killed the Franks who were in them.
And he came and encamped against Edessa for some time,
and was not able to conquer it.
And he left it and went to Tell Bashir,
which was also held by the Franks,
and he was not able to conquer it either.
And when he left it and went to Aleppo,
Ridwan, the lord of Aleppo, shut the gates against him.
And he left Aleppo and went to Damascus,
and the Emir Toghtekin came out to meet him,
and showed him affection.
And afterwards he was afraid of him,
lest he should act treacherously toward him and take control of Damascus.
And he, Toghtekin, sent to the Franks,
and made peace with them,
and treated Mawdud with contempt.
